statement: Premise assessment for U029: the strongest available quantitative signal is the 10.8% temporal-evidence-leakage rate of a hybrid RAG baseline under point-in-time conditions, i.e. roughly one in nine retrieved items violated the time boundary, alongside capability statements that current architectures cannot tell whether a retrieved provision remains in force and that corpora containing only current versions make past-date queries anachronistic, plus a roughly 15-point accuracy drop on present-day questions with an updated corpus. These make a non-trivial version-confusion problem plausible but do not measure it for amended clauses: the leakage metric concerns evidence published after an as-of date rather than superseded clause versions, the domain is financial filings rather than statutes, and no retrieved work reports a version-level failure rate for any retriever on amended legal text. The rate must therefore be measured descriptively before any mechanism comparison is interpreted.

evidence.quote: reducing temporal evidence leakage from 10.8% to 1.7%
